comments.author: Marco Reyes
comments.body: Chaos test injecting ±500ms skew no longer refills early. Closed.

content.text: Chaos test injecting ±500ms skew no longer refills early. Closed.

API rate limiter windows reset earlier than the configured 60-second bucket when nodes disagree on wall-clock time. Clients suddenly get a full quota again mid-window, then slam into 429s when traffic lands on a node with a correct clock.

Expected behavior is a fixed window anchored to a shared time source so remaining quota decreases monotonically within the window. Observed: under ~180ms skew between api-node-3 and the Redis-backed counter host, local windowStart calculations fall into the prior bucket and refill prematurely.
Root hypothesis: each node computes windowStart = floor(localNow / 60s) instead of using Redis TIME or a logical bucket id from the store. Clock skew directly shifts the bucket index.
Bursty clients appear to break through limits, then trigger false-positive abuse alerts on the next correctly timed node hop.
